# Remepy secures $36m funding for Hybrid Drug pipeline expansion

The latest round brings the total capital raised by Remepy to $62m\.

Remepy develops hybrid drugs through partnerships with pharmaceutical companies\. Credit: Gorodenkoff / Shutterstock\.com\.

Remepy has closed a $36m Series A financing round to accelerate its pharmaceutical co-development partnerships and expand its hybrid drug pipeline\.

The proceeds will also be used to fund Remepy’s lead product Hybridopa’s global Phase III clinical trial targeting Parkinson’s disease \(PD\)\. It is set to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026\.

#### Discover B2B Marketing That Performs

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms\.

Find out more

The latest funding brings the total capital raised by the company to $62m\.

The Series A round was led by OG Venture Partners and M Ventures, Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s corporate strategic venture arm\.

Other new and existing backers include NFX, Qumra Capital, Tadmor Group, TechAviv, and Vine Ventures\.

Remepy develops Hybrid Drugs through partnerships with pharmaceutical companies\.

These drugs combine prescription medicines with personalised, AI-driven therapeutic applications, aiming to integrate pharmacology with adaptive physical, cognitive, and behavioural interventions into a single treatment regimen\.

The company stated that the Hybrid Drug model has gained traction, supported by evolving US regulatory frameworks for drug-software combination products\.

Remepy recently disclosed a strategic partnership with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany to develop hybrid drugs for multiple indications, beginning with rare tumours\.

Hybridopa, it’s lead programme for Parkinson’s disease, has reported positive Phase IIa clinical data regarding both motor and non-motor symptom improvement\.

It remains an investigational product and has not received approval from the US Food and Drug Administration\.

Remepy co-CEOs Michal Tsur and Or Shoval said: “We believe medicine is entering a new era, where every breakthrough drug will be paired with personalised intelligence to maximise its impact for every patient\.

“Over the past year, we’ve demonstrated that this vision is achievable through clinical validation, peer-reviewed science, regulatory alignment, and partnerships with leading pharmaceutical companies\.

“This financing allows us to advance Phase III of Hybridopa for Parkinson’s disease, and expand the hybrid drug model across multiple therapeutic areas\.”

# Remepy secures $36m funding for hybrid drug pipeline expansion

The latest round brings the total capital raised by Remepy to $62m\.

Remepy develops hybrid drugs through partnerships with pharmaceutical companies\. Credit: Gorodenkoff / Shutterstock\.com\.

Remepy has closed a $36m Series A financing round to accelerate its pharmaceutical co-development partnerships and expand its hybrid drug pipeline\.

The proceeds will also be used to fund Remepy’s lead product Hybridopa’s global Phase III clinical trial targeting Parkinson’s disease \(PD\)\. It is set to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026\.

Other new and existing backers include NFX, Qumra Capital, Tadmor Group, TechAviv, and Vine Ventures\.

Remepy develops Hybrid Drugs through partnerships with pharmaceutical companies\.

These drugs combine prescription medicines with personalised, AI-driven therapeutic applications, aiming to integrate pharmacology with adaptive physical, cognitive, and behavioural interventions into a single treatment regimen\.

The company stated that the Hybrid Drug model has gained traction, supported by evolving US regulatory frameworks for drug-software combination products\.

Remepy recently disclosed a strategic partnership with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany to develop hybrid drugs for multiple indications, beginning with rare tumours\.

Hybridopa, it’s lead programme for Parkinson’s disease, has reported positive Phase IIa clinical data regarding both motor and non-motor symptom improvement\.

It remains an investigational product and has not received approval from the US Food and Drug Administration\.

Remepy co-CEOs Michal Tsur and Or Shoval said: “We believe medicine is entering a new era, where every breakthrough drug will be paired with personalised intelligence to maximise its impact for every patient\.

“Over the past year, we’ve demonstrated that this vision is achievable through clinical validation, peer-reviewed science, regulatory alignment, and partnerships with leading pharmaceutical companies\.

“This financing allows us to advance Phase III of Hybridopa for Parkinson’s disease, and expand the hybrid drug model across multiple therapeutic areas\.”

Remepy, a pioneer in hybrid drugs, announced that it closed a $10 million seed investment round, totaling $15 million when combined with earlier funding\. This funding round was led by NFX and was joined by Vine Ventures, PsyMed Ventures, Supernode Ventures, and Firstime Ventures, while joining previous pre-seed lead investors TechAviv and Fresh\.fund, Samsung Next, StageNext Fund, and 97212 Ventures\.

Remepy’s new hybrid drugs combine traditional drugs with *digital molecules*\. The digital molecules are therapeutic interventions that trigger physiological effects \(aka MOAs, Mechanisms of Action\) through the brain\. These physiological changes have been known to enhance the effectiveness of traditional drugs\.

These digital molecules are designed for hybrid drug experiences\. They are based on noninvasive cognitive, psychological, and behavioral interventions that follow the principles of sensory integration, sensory substitution, and sensory deprivation\. These interventions trigger multiple unique mechanisms of action, including changes to brain connectivity in important brain areas, changes to immune system blood biomarkers, and important behavioral changes\.

Remepy has already demonstrated the effects of its digital molecule interventions in clinical trials using extensive fMRI imaging, blood and saliva samples analysis, and standardized questionnaires\. And it is among the first in the world to show that its patent-pending digital therapies can modulate blood biomarkers\.

Many diseases are also better treated by combining drugs with non-pharmacological interventions\. And Remepy is making such combinations standardized, accessible and personalized at scale using its digital molecules\.

Remepy targets neurodegenerative diseases, cancer, autoimmune diseases, and degenerative eye diseases\. Its approach creates a new market for hybrid medications and a new world of data and IP assets for pharmaceutical companies\.

**KEY QUOTES:**

*“As a physician and drug developer, it is fascinating for me to see Remepy’s clinical data, which shows how these unique non-invasive digital interventions can modulate the immune system, make significant changes to brain plasticity, and drive behavioral changes\. Remepy’s product has the potential to enhance immunotherapy for cancer, or improve existing drug therapy for neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s Disease and MCI \(Mild Cognitive Impairment\)\. These proprietary digital-drug combinations could significantly improve patient outcomes and create tangible value for patients and healthcare systems\.”*

- **Dr\. Danny Bar Zohar, Merck’s Global head of R&D and Chief Medical Officer**

*“I am thrilled that Dr\. Danny Bar Zohar has joined us as a board member\. Many industries have transformed by adopting a hybrid product approach, integrating new technology with traditional products\.” Co-CEO Or Shoval added: “I am particularly excited about the prospects of improving Parkinson’s Disease patients’ lives with a hybrid PD drug that will better address cognitive, movement, speech, sleeping and psychological symptoms and has the potential of disease modification with changes to brain connectivity\.”*

- **Dr\. Michal Tsur, Remepy Co-CEO**

*“Remepy’s vision of enhancing drugs with digital companions is groundbreaking and their clinical proof that such enhancement is possible is incredibly exciting\. Remepy has an experienced team of entrepreneurs and world-class scientists that are defining a new category in pharma\.”*

- **Gigi Levy-Weiss, Managing Partner at NFX**

Michal Tsur, co-founder and co-CEO, Remepy, and Naftali Bennett, former Israeli Prime Minister

Remepy

Combining software with medicine to unlock an entire new market for “hybrid drugs” is the vision driving Israeli startup Remepy\. As many diseases are better treated by combining drugs with non-pharmacological interventions, Remepy is making such combinations standardized, accessible and personalized at scale with the use of its “digital molecules\.” These are digitized, evidence-based therapeutic interventions that trigger physiological effects that have been known to enhance the effectiveness of traditional drugs\.

Michal Tsur, Remepy co-founder and co-CEO, calls its hybrid approach “a very big revolution, similar to what happened with immunotherapy,” which transformed the world of pharma by harnessing the immune system to attack tumors\. “We are using digital tools in order to harness the brain to drive physiological effects that are synergistic with drugs,” explains Tsur\.

Remepy announced last month that it has successfully closed a $10 million seed investment round, which together with earlier funding totals $15 million\. The round was led by NFX, joined by Vine Ventures, PsyMed Ventures, Supernode Ventures and Firstime Ventures, joining previous pre-seed lead investor TechAviv as well as Fresh\.fund, Samsung Next, StageNext Fund and 97212 Ventures\. Remepy also announced that Danny Bar Zohar, Merck’s Global head of R&D and Chief Medical Officer, and former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, have joined its board of directors\.

Tsur is a well-known Israeli serial entrepreneur\. In 1999, together with Bennet and other founders, she launched Cyota, a pioneer in the anti-fraud market which was sold to RSA in 2005 for $145 million\. She then co-founded Kaltura, a successful open-source video platform which was valued at $1\.24 billion when it went public in 2021\. A year later, together with Or Shoval and Professor Amir Amedi, Tsur founded Remepy\.

Amedi is the founding director of The Baruch Ivcher Institute for Brain, Cognition & Technology and The Ruth and Meir Rosental Brain Imaging Center \(MRI\) and Professor in the School of Psychology in Reichman University, Israel\. These research centers aim to build on insights from basic neuroscience and turn them into impactful technologies that can improve medical outcomes\.

MORE FROM FORBES ADVISOR

Remepy was born out of this research effort and is among the first in the world to demonstrate in early clinical studies the physiological effects of digital interventions, according to Tsur\. “The data from our trials validated our ability to change brain connectivity in memory, navigation, and emotion control areas of the brain, as well as optimize levels of immune biomarkers in blood and saliva\. Our psychological questionnaires validated our ability to reduce stress and anxiety and depression compared to control groups,” says Tsur\.

Remepy’s approach improves patient care in a variety of ways\. First and foremost, it scales up and standardizes proven complementary therapies by adapting them to a single, personalized digital application\. Many patients do not have access to these therapies and are treated only with drugs\. For patients receiving the best available care, different therapies are provided by different therapists and are not integrated and standardized\. With Remepy’s approach, all the complementary therapies are integrated in one application running on a device in the patient’s pocket, increasing convenience, engagement and personalization\. An additional benefit of Remepy’s approach is that patient data is collected continuously, allowing for adaptation of the treatment and, across patients, for gaining new insights\.

Hybrid drugs are tested initially on humans, skipping a number of early phases in the traditional process of drug development\. As such, the time it takes for a new drug to reach the market—typically 10 years—could be cut in half, according to Tsur\. The regulatory process is quite straight forward as hybrid drugs could be considered a medical device/drug combination\. Remepy intends to go to market either by combining their software with a pharma generic product or by combining the software with existing drugs or drugs that are in the process of development\.

Remepy is targeting diseases where meaningful changes to brain connectivity, changes to the immune system and behavioral changes are synergistic with drug effects\. Starting with Parkinson’s Disease, Remepy will explore bringing its hybrid drugs to neurodegenerative diseases, cancer, autoimmune diseases, and degenerative eye diseases\.

“We're building a broad platform for launching digital molecules and the hybrid drugs that correspond to them,” says Tsur\.

Just as drivers use mobile apps such as Waze for a better navigation experience, or Fitbit fitness tracker devices are worn to enhance exercise outcomes, an Israeli biotech startup believes that in the future patients will be prescribed traditional drugs coupled with personally tailored software applications to optimize their effectiveness and improve medical outcomes\.

Founded in 2022 by Dr\. Michal Tsur, co-founder of video platform provider Kaltura, and Or Shoval, Remepy is developing tailored therapeutic software for mobile applications that the startup says can unlock and trigger brain functions that modulate the immune system and are synergetic with traditional drugs\.

The idea is to create a platform that connects the mind and body through cognitive-behavioral exercises, guided meditations and other practices drawn from neuroscience, such as multisensory conditioning\.

The startup announced on Wednesday that it raised $10 million from a seed funding round taking its total financing to $15 million\. It seeks to use the funds to pioneer and bring the “first hybrid drug \[combination of digital therapeutic software with drugs\] to the market\.”

The startup believes that many neurodegenerative and autoimmune diseases, including cancer and Parkinson’s Disease, are better treated by combining drugs with non-pharmacological digital treatments\.

The funding round was led by venture capital firm NFX\. Investors that joined the round are Vine Ventures, Psymed Ventures, Supernode Ventures and Firstime Ventures\. Other investors include Tech Aviv as well as fresh\.fund, and 97212 Ventures\.

Remepy co-CEOs Michal Tsur \(left\) and Or Shoval \(right\) together with chief scientific officer Prof\. Amir Amedi\. \(Courtesy\)

“We are leveraging the power of digital interactions with our brain to cause physiological changes that are synergetic with drugs,” Tsur, who serves as Remepy’s co-CEO told The Times of Israel during a phone interview\. “We can trigger different processes in the brain that have to do with brain connectivity, modulating the immune system, and activating the reward system which are extremely synergetic with the influence of drugs and are intended to improve outcomes\.”

“We focus on psychological behavioral and cognitive interactions that trigger the brain mechanisms that are synergetic with many types of drugs,” Tsur added\.

Pharma giant Merck’s global head of R&D and chief medical officer Dr\. Danny Bar Zohar has joined the startup’s board of directors, Remepy said\. That’s after former prime minister Naftali Bennett, who co-founded fintech startup Cyota with Tsur, joined the board in February\.

Tsur said that the digital app has shown encouraging results in pilot studies and clinical trials run with about 200 patients such as decreasing depression, anxiety and insomnia, and improving resilience and biomarkers related to chronic stress and inflammation\.

As part of the trials, the startup said it used extensive brain imaging, blood and saliva samples analysis and standardized questionnaires to show that its patent-pending digital therapies can modulate blood biomarkers\.

File: Illustration of an autoimmune disease, with antibodies attacking neurons \(Dr\.\_Microbe via iStock by Getty Images\)

“As a physician and drug developer, it is fascinating for me to see Remepy’s clinical data, which shows how these unique non-invasive digital interventions can modulate the immune system, make significant changes to brain plasticity, and drive behavioral changes,” said Bar Zohar\. “Remepy’s product has the potential to enhance immunotherapy for cancer, or improve existing drug therapy for neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s Disease and MCI \(Mild Cognitive Impairment\)\.”

“These proprietary digital-drug combinations could significantly improve patient outcomes and create tangible value for patients and healthcare systems,” he added\.

Tsur said the startup seeks to partner with pharma companies to integrate its digital therapeutic applications with both proprietary drugs and generic drugs\.

“In such a difficult period of war for many people in Israel some of us feel that healing also has to do with building, innovating and thinking,” she said\. “We feel fortunate that what we are doing is not only building in order to heal, but we are going to be building something that has the potential to heal severe diseases\.”

# Remepy Raises $36 Million Series A To Advance Hybridopa Phase III And Hybrid Drug Pipeline

By Amit Chowdhry Today at 4:18 PM

Remepy has raised $36 million in Series A funding to expand its Hybrid Drug pipeline, accelerate pharmaceutical partnerships, and fund global Phase III development of Hybridopa for Parkinson’s disease\. The financing brings the company’s total capital raised to $62 million\. O\.G\. Venture Partners and M Ventures, the strategic venture arm of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, led the round\. Investors also included NFX, Vine Ventures, Qumra Capital, TechAviv, 97212 Ventures, Fresh Fund, PsyMed Ventures, Tadmor Group, Key1 Capital, and IT-Farm\.

Remepy is developing what it calls Hybrid Drugs, which combine prescription medicines with personalized AI-driven therapeutic applications\. The approach combines pharmacology with adaptive physical, cognitive, and behavioral interventions through a standard prescription model\.

The company has also entered a strategic collaboration with Merck KGaA to develop Hybrid Drugs across multiple indications, beginning with rare tumors\.

Remepy’s lead program, Hybridopa, is being developed for Parkinson’s disease\. The company said its Phase IIa results demonstrated improvements in motor and non-motor symptoms and were supported by peer-reviewed research into the biological mechanisms behind the treatment\.

Global Phase III development is scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026\. Hybridopa remains investigational and has not been approved by the FDA\.

**KEY QUOTES:**

*“We believe medicine is entering a new era, where every breakthrough drug will be paired with personalized intelligence to maximize its impact for every patient\. Over the past year, we’ve demonstrated that this vision is achievable through clinical validation, peer-reviewed science, regulatory alignment, and partnerships with leading pharmaceutical companies\. This financing allows us to advance Phase III of Hybridopa for Parkinson’s disease, and expand the Hybrid Drug model across multiple therapeutic areas\.”*

**Michal Tsur, Ph\.D\., and Or Shoval, Co-CEOs of Remepy**

*“We’re excited to lead Remepy’s Series A and support an exceptional team pioneering a new category of medicine\. By bringing together biotechnology, AI, and digital health, Remepy is redefining how medicines are developed and delivered\. With compelling clinical data, growing regulatory momentum, and strong validation from leading pharmaceutical partners, we believe Hybrid Drugs have the potential to transform patient care\.”*

**Ziv Kop, Managing Partner at O\.G\. Venture Partners**

*“Remepy’s pioneering Hybrid Drugs approach reflects the growing importance and applicability of integrating AI into the delivery of health and physical medicines\. Our investment from M Ventures is intended to further enable the company, underscoring our belief that this new class of medicine, that combines innovative therapeutics with AI-driven, patient-centered care, has the potential to redefine medicine\.”*

**Dr\. Eyal Ben Ami, Scientific Lead at M Ventures**

# Singapore start-up Ropedia raises US$22 mil in pre-Series A round for robot-training data

The robotics data company has raised US$30 million so far, and will use the latest funds to gather more training data, increase device production and expand in Singapore and the US\.

Ropedia, a Singapore start-up that supplies training data for robots and physical artificial intelligence systems, has raised US$22 million \($28\.4 million\) in a pre-Series A funding round\.

It did not identify the investors in the latest round, saying only that it was led by venture firms with experience in AI, deep technology and infrastructure in Southeast Asia\.

The deal brings its total funding to US$30 million\. An earlier round included investors and individuals connected to Google, Andreessen Horowitz, Nvidia and Amazon, according to the company\.

Ropedia's proprietary wearable devices record first-person video, depth, movement and audio as people carry out physical tasks\. The company processes that information into training material for developers seeking to teach robots how to perform tasks in real-world settings\. It offers the data through its Xperience-10M product and customised services\.

\"A robot can't play baseball by watching a video any more than you could learn to ride a bike by reading about it\. The robot must understand what it's like to grip a bat and know the timing it takes to hit a ball\. That's the information Ropedia's technology provides, and it's why this investment matters,\" says Zhaoxi Chen, CEO and co-founder of Ropedia\.

He continues: \"Our technology lets robots capture the experience and real judgment it will take for them to move through the world\. If we get all that right, the robots will leave the beta stage and start doing real work, first in factories, then at home, with families\.\"

According to Ropedia, its approach can reduce data-collection costs by as much as 50 times compared with traditional methods\.

Its wearable device has entered mass production, and the company is already working with more than 20 robotics and foundation-model companies in North America, China and Singapore\.

Ropedia will use the fresh funds to expand data collection in Southeast Asia and North America, increase production of its wearable devices and grow its teams in Singapore and the US\.

It also plans to add tools for annotating and checking data, strengthen its compliance systems and expand research into data foundation models and world models\.

Ropedia was founded in the second half of 2025 by Chen, chief technology officer Fangzhou Hong and chief scientist Ziwei Liu, an associate professor at Nanyang Technological University\.

# Whatnot funding round lifts founders’ wealth as live shopping gains traction in U\.S\.

Live shopping platforms are drawing fresh investor attention as real-time auctions expand across the U\.S\. Whatnot’s latest capital raise values the Los Angeles company at $20 billion and pushes its two co-founders into multibillionaire territory\.

## Highlights

- Whatnot's $545 million funding round boosts its valuation to $20 billion, significantly increasing founders Grant LaFontaine and Logan Head's paper wealth\.
- Bloomberg Billionaires Index reports LaFontaine and Head are now each worth over $2\.8 billion following the latest capital raise\.
- The funding and valuation jump highlight growing momentum for live commerce in the U\.S\. and signal strong investor confidence in interactive mobile auction platforms\.

## Funding round and valuation jump

As reported by Bloomberg, citing Bloomberg Billionaires Index, Whatnot’s latest funding round increases the paper wealth of Chief Executive Officer Grant LaFontaine and Chief Technology Officer Logan Head to more than $2\.8 billion each\. The index is valuing their fortunes for the first time after the company announced on Friday that it raised $545 million\.

The Los Angeles-based e-commerce company says the round values Whatnot at $20 billion\. The funding comes after last week’s raise and reflects investor backing for the app’s fast-paced live auction model\.

## Momentum for live commerce in U\.S\.

Whatnot’s valuation increase underscores the growing appeal of live shopping formats in the U\.S\., where consumers are increasingly using mobile platforms to buy through interactive auctions\. The company’s latest raise also signals that investors see further expansion potential in the segment\.

The gains for LaFontaine and Head place both founders among newly minted multibillionaires as the sector attracts more attention from capital markets\. Their holdings rise alongside Whatnot’s higher valuation, linking founder wealth directly to the company’s latest financing milestone\.

# India’s FinTech Rises Globally as Bengaluru Claims Nearly 70% of Total Funding

### **Overview**

- India’s fintech sector raised over $2\.2 billion across 100-plus funding rounds\.

- Late-stage fintechs received more than 70% of total H1 funding\.

- Bengaluru dominated funding, while Accel emerged as the most active investor\.

India’s fintech sector continued to attract strong investor interest in the first half of 2026, even as funding decisions became more selective\. The sector raised more than $2\.2 billion across 100-plus funding rounds, marking the strongest half-year funding performance since H1 2023\.

The latest numbers come as global venture capital remains cautious following the funding peak of 2021\. For India, the H1 2026 performance points to continued investor confidence, but also shows a market where larger, established fintech companies are attracting a greater share of capital\.

India was the world’s third-largest fintech funding market in 2025, behind the United States and the United Kingdom, retaining that position for the second consecutive year\.

## **Larger Fintechs Take the Lead**

The biggest funding round of H1 2026 came from CRED, which raised $900 million\. The transaction was significantly larger than most deals in the market and underlined the growing concentration of capital among established fintech companies\.

More than 70% of the funding raised during the first half of 2026 went to late-stage fintechs\. Companies including CRED, Weaver Services, Juspay, Ecofy Finance and Namdev Finvest were among the beneficiaries\.

The trend reflects a change in investor behavior\. The market is no longer driven mainly by the number of companies raising money\. Investors are putting more emphasis on proven business models, scalability and clearer routes to profitability\.

The same pattern was visible in 2025, when Indian fintech companies raised more than $2 billion, despite a decline in the number of funding rounds\.

## **Lending and Payments Dominate Funding**

Lending was the largest-funded fintech segment in H1 2026, followed by Payments\. Together, the two sectors accounted for more than three-quarters of total funding\.

The dominance of these segments reflects the scale of India’s digital financial services market\. At the same time, investor interest is spreading to other parts of the ecosystem\. Wealthtech was also among the sectors attracting attention during the period\.

India’s fintech industry has expanded significantly beyond digital payments\. Companies now operate across lending, wealth management, insurtech, embedded finance and financial infrastructure, giving investors a wider range of opportunities\.

## **Bengaluru Accounts for Nearly 70% of Funding**

The funding remained heavily concentrated geographically\. Bengaluru accounted for around 70% of total fintech funding in H1 2026, retaining its position as India’s biggest fintech funding hub\. Mumbai was the second-highest funding city\.

Bengaluru’s lead reflects the depth of its startup and technology ecosystem, along with its established investor networks and concentration of fintech companies\. While fintech businesses have expanded across the country, a large share of institutional capital continues to flow through India’s major technology hubs\.

## **Accel Was the Most Active Investor**

Accel was the most active backer in India’s fintech space during H1 2026\. Institutional investors remained the most active investor group overall, while domestic investors participated across multiple financing stages\.

Meanwhile, foreign investors seemed to lean more strongly toward mature fintech firms, especially around the growth stage\. The role of corporate and strategic investors also increased during this period, as they became more active\.

This shifting blend of investors looks like yet another cue that the market is inching toward higher maturity\. More fintech companies are raising capital not only for expansion but also from investors seeking strategic opportunities across financial services and technology\.

## **IPOs and Secondary Deals Add to Activity**

The first half of 2026 also saw activity beyond traditional funding rounds\. Kissht and TurtleMint completed fintech IPOs, taking the number of fintech IPOs during the period to two\.

The sector also recorded the largest secondary transaction of Rs\. 5,352 crore involving Groww\. Secondary transactions, IPOs and acquisitions are becoming an increasingly important part of the fintech funding ecosystem as investors and founders look for liquidity and exit opportunities\.

These transactions also offer a clearer picture of how the industry is maturing\. Capital is no longer entering fintech companies only through early- and growth-stage fundraising\. Public listings and secondary transactions are becoming part of the broader capital cycle\.

## **India’s FinTech Market Enters More Disciplined Phase**

The fintech landscape in India remains one of the most vital destinations for investment across the globe\. The $2\.2 billion-plus invested in more than 100 deals in H1 2026 indicates strong investor interest\.

However, how that money was allocated is what counts\. Over 70% of this investment went to later-stage firms, with Lending and Payments receiving well over three-quarters of the total investment\. Close to 70% of this funding came from Bengaluru alone, while the $900 million raised by CRED was the biggest single deal\.

This trend marks something of a paradigm shift in India’s fintech space\. Investors now seem more selective and are paying closer attention to the basics of the business and its ability to expand steadily\.

The Indian fintech market still has big potential, but the spotlight is probably going to move toward how companies build sustainable operations, instead of trying to raise capital quickly\.

# Chinese start-up ModelBest raises significant funding as edge AI competition intensifies

Beijing-based ModelBest secures a major C\+ Series funding round, highlighting the growing investor confidence in on-device AI amidst rising competition from tech giants like Tencent and Apple\.Beijing-based ModelBest has\.\.\.

Beijing-based ModelBest secures a major C\+ Series funding round, highlighting the growing investor confidence in on-device AI amidst rising competition from tech giants like Tencent and Apple\.

Beijing-based ModelBest has completed a C\+ Series funding round, taking its total fundraising this year to 5 billion yuan, or about $740m, as investors continue to back start-ups building AI that can run directly on devices\. Shanghai Mejoy Capital, one of the investors, said the round valued the company at 20 billion yuan, although it did not disclose how much was raised in the latest tranche\. According to the figures shared by investors, the deal underlines rising confidence in on-device AI, which promises lower latency, less dependence on remote servers and better privacy\.

Noah Intelligence has been tracking this shift as a live signal of enterprise adoption, infrastructure choices and buyer demand, where on-device AI is increasingly tied to cost, privacy and deployment constraints\.

The broader shift is being driven by the limits of cloud-based AI, where more demanding tasks still need distant data centres\. That adds cost and delay, while also creating privacy concerns when user data has to leave the handset or laptop\. As a result, developers are increasingly pursuing local, or edge, AI models that can handle more work on the device itself, even as they continue to build larger frontier systems\.

ModelBest has positioned itself as one of China’s most visible players in this area\. In May, it said its MiniCPM5-1B model, with 1 billion parameters, had been trained entirely on Huawei’s Ascend chips, reflecting a wider domestic push to make better use of locally produced AI hardware\. Independent model listings and coverage of the release say the model is designed for constrained devices, with some versions packaged for laptops and edge systems, and that it is intended to work without cloud dependence\.

The company is not alone in targeting this market\. Tencent-backed StepFun recently unveiled Step Edge, a family of on-device models aimed at low latency and offline operation, and followed that with a smartphone concept built around autonomous AI agents\. Apple is also pursuing a mixed strategy, combining external partners for high-end tasks with its own on-device models, while testing technology that claims to run much larger language models locally on an iPhone\. The competition suggests that edge AI is moving from a niche technical ambition to a central battleground in consumer technology\.

Shanghai Mejoy Capital, one of the investors, said the round valued the company at 20 billion yuan, although it did not disclose how much was raised in the latest tranche\. According to the figures shared by investors, the deal underlines rising confidence in on-device AI, which promises lower latency, less dependence on remote servers and better privacy\.
